A simulated brick world had this hidden rule:
In this world the agent's observation shows the target shifted: the target, missing, extra and target-height channels are rolled 4 columns toward higher x, wrapping around. The world, its designs and scoring are as described.

Below is what an AI scientist wrote during a search in that world: its analysis at every round, in order, and the
name and hypothesis of the trial it ended with. Does the text, anywhere, state the rule?
- "yes": it states the rule's substance (what is changed and how).
- "partly": it identifies the right kind of change but not its specifics.
- "no": anything else.

## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
There is only one result so far. The starting architecture learned to choose DONE before placing anything, so both seeds scored 0. The traces explain why. The target heights the agent sees are the real design shifted cyclically by 4 columns (X/2) along x, and the rows are unchanged. This holds for every row of both designs (for example 00220000 is seen as 00000022, and 00100011 as 00110010). Rewards and actions use the real, unshifted positions; the untrained trace's rewards confirm this. A translation-equivariant convnet with a 5x5 receptive field therefore sees no target signal near where it would place a brick. Every placement looks negative and DONE (reward 0) wins. The default recipe also gives only about 32 updates. My first test is to give the network an x-rolled copy of the observation. This copy lines things up whether only the target channels or the whole observation are shifted. I also test a learned spatial-mixing layer that could undo any fixed permutation, and a recipe with more updates.

### Round 2
The observed target is rolled by X/2 along x. Diagnostic design 1 has target cells at columns 2–3, but the observation shows them at columns 6–7. The starting convnet could not match target and build locally, so it learned to choose DONE at once. Adding a rolled copy of the input fixed this: r1c1 scored 0.59. The learned token-mix (r1c3) did not learn at all: it stayed at 0, probably because the noisy initial mixing gave no clean signal. With the same network, the recipe giving about 2.5x more updates (r1c2) raised dev success to 0.89, and both seeds scored above 0.85. That gap is much larger than seed noise, so update count is a strong lever. Training took about 66 s, far under the 900 s limit, so there is room for many more, smaller updates. The remaining failures are probably about build order and when to choose DONE, since mean IoU is already 0.97. This round tests two further update-count recipes and one change that adds more context to the network.

### Round 3
The observed target is shifted by X/2 along x. Diagnostic design 1 shows this: target columns 2-3 appear at 6-7. Adding a rolled copy of the observation fixed the shift (r1c1: 0.59). The learned token-mix did not learn the shift and failed (0.00). Going from about 31 to about 77 updates (128 envs, 3 epochs) raised dev success to 0.89, and both seeds were stable. More aggressive recipes with 64 envs were unstable: one seed of r2c1 and both seeds of r2c2 collapsed to an immediate DONE. Random early placements earn negative reward while DONE earns 0, so fast updates can lock in DONE. The bigger net (r2c3, 1.37x compute) scored 0.74 with tight seeds and was still improving, so training is limited by samples and updates, not capacity. With 6 trials left, refine r1c2's recipe: longer credit horizon, more samples per update without the small-batch noise, and a higher learning rate.

### Round 4
The roll-concat input was the change that unlocked learning. In this world the target channels arrive rolled by X/2 along x, and the diagnostic traces confirm this. With the network fixed, recipe changes gave the gains. r1c2 scored 0.89 with 128 envs and 3 epochs. Three single changes then each scored 0.91 to 0.93: gamma 0.99 (0.906), lr 0.0015 (0.921), and 2 epochs with ent 0.02 (0.928). Each of these gains is within seed noise, but all three point the same way, so they may add up. Smaller batches (64 envs) made training unstable: 2 epochs with ent 0.01 collapsed to DONE. Making the network bigger (dilated block plus global broadcast) cost samples and did worse. The learned token-mix failed. In this last round I combine the gains that point the same way, push further toward fresh samples with 1 epoch, and test lr 0.0015 on the current best.

## Trial it ended with
name: r1c2 + 2 epochs at 128 envs, ent 0.02
hypothesis: Change: r1c2's network with 2 PPO epochs instead of 3. The batch stays at 128 envs and 2048 samples, and the entropy coefficient rises to 0.02. That gives about 227k samples and 111 updates instead of 157k and 77. r2c2 collapsed to DONE with 64 envs. The larger batch and extra entropy should stop that early collapse while keeping the gain from more samples. Refuted if a seed collapses to DONE or dev success is not above 0.89.

Return a JSON object: "verdict" ("yes", "partly" or "no") and "evidence" (at most 80 words, quoting the text and
naming the round it comes from).
